searches.note: Fifteen searches of a share of twenty eight, thirteen left unspent for the run's shared allowance. Two searches served the whole group (the VDP Mittelrhein association's founding and chairs; the members' years of joining) and are counted with Toni Jost and Ratzenberger. One wasted search for the Bernstein outside the VDP's domain returned nothing and is counted with Lanius-Knab. Most were restricted to the VDP's own domain and read as summaries. No fetch tried. The wein.plus magazine address carries the living grower's name and is listed here only, never in the fragment.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the classification, the grapes, the sites with their heights, aspects and soils, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the dates the stories turn on (the VDP Mittelrhein association of 1987 and its chairs, each house's year of joining, Toni Jost's 1831 and 1953, Lanius-Knab's 1991 and 1995, Weingart's 1960s and 1996, Matthias Müller's handover), then to the sites on the VDP's own pages, then to tasting notes for the two glasses the author had written from the style of the site.

Where a site's figures differed from the VDP's own page (the Bernstein Am Lauerbaum, the Feuerlay) the VDP's figures were taken; where a claim rested on nothing read (the Schönburg opposite the Lauerbaum, the Walkenberg's soil, the Engelstein's iron, the Feuerlay as the warmest exposure, the etymologies of Hahnenhof and Feuerlay) it was cut.

tested: 1831: the VDP's Weinberg.online and Weinpaket pages, written from the house (grown Riesling at Bacharach since 1831, seventh generation); kept, hedged as the house's account.
1953: the VDP's Weinpaket page gives the joining of Toni Jost of Bacharach with Weller of Walluf, through the marriage of the grandparents of the present owner; kept, spouses unnamed.
1987: the VDP's region page gives seven Bacharach estates founding the association in 1987, and the VDP gives Toni Jost a member since 1987; worded as membership since that year.

The Hahn: the VDP lists the Bacharacher Hahn as the estate's monopole, Erste Lage, and Im Hahn as Grosse Lage, about two hectares of dark weathered Devonian slate, south to south east, 65 to 70 per cent.

The label: Falstaff lists Bacharach Im Hahn Riesling GG for 2017 to 2023, and a critic's database prints Bacharacher Hahn Riesling Grosses Gewächs for 2015 and Bacharacher Im Hahn for 2023, so the plan's words are the older form.
Others: Falstaff lists a Walluf Walkenberg Riesling VDP Grosses Gewächs (2012) and a Bacharach Im Hahn Spätburgunder GG (2018, 2020, 2021); both stand.
The questions: one right answer each, options of one kind; the distractors 1831 and 1987 are the record's own dates and teach. House rules: no living name, no price, no score, British, no dash.

tested: 1987 and the chair: the VDP's region page gives the association's founding in 1987 by seven Bacharach estates and the father of the house as chairman from 1998 to 2010, and the son as chairman since; the VDP gives Ratzenberger a member since 1987.

The St. Jost: the VDP's page gives 170 to 200 metres, about 60 per cent falling south, Devonian slate under windblown sand from volcanic eruptions in the Neuwied Basin more than ten thousand years ago.
The Wolfshöhle as a second Grosse Lage of the house: the VDP's Weinberg.online lists both; Falstaff lists a Wolfshöhle Grosses Gewächs (2012) and Vinous one for 2020.
The Sekt: the house's own words on its VDP page (traditional method, long lees ageing, for many years) and Falstaff's Riesling brut listings.
Stainless steel: Vinous and a Swiss importer's profile (only Pinot Noir sees wood).
The three hundred years: the tourism and importer pages give the family as the third generation in the old Hütwohl estate, so the long history belongs to the building, not the family.
The questions: one answer each; the explanations teach the Boppard loop and the chair's years.

The three hundred years, the mixed farm, the turn to wine in the twentieth century and the handover shortly before 2000 to the son and his wife: the Wines of Germany profile and a tourism page (the late 1990s); kept, the people unnamed.

The Mandelstein: the VDP's page gives south south east, 70 to 170 metres, 45 to 70 per cent, weathered Devonian slate; the house's own words on its VDP page name the Mandelstein GG the wine closest to its heart, from its oldest parcel directly below a wall.
The sites the house works: the VDP lists the Fässerlay, Feuerlay, Mandelstein, Ohlenberg, Engelstein and An der Rabenlei; the Grosse Lage rank of the Ohlenberg and the Engelstein was not shown.
The glass: left as the author wrote it on a Meininger note and a critic's note; not re-tested.
The questions: one answer each; the 1995 distractor is Lanius-Knab's year, confirmed.

1991 and the two hundred and fifty years: the VDP's page and the Mittelrhein tourism pages (in the family about 250 years; continuously enlarged since 1991 by the present head); kept, hedged.

Am Lauerbaum: the VDP's page gives S, 80 to 170 metres, 65 to 70 per cent, Devonian slate, Riesling and Spätburgunder, and the house's words: the Lauerbaum is the choice part of the Bernstein, which lies in a hollow like an amphitheatre facing due south.
Riesling's share: about 85 per cent on the tourism page and the VDP's.
The label: Falstaff lists Engehöll Bernstein Am Lauerbaum Riesling GG (2015 to 2023), Engehöller Bernstein Riesling EL trocken (2018) and Oberwesel Oelsberg Riesling GG (2016).
The Schönburg opposite the Lauerbaum: nothing read sets it there.
The questions: one answer each; the story question re-worded to what the sources say of 1991.
